core: Both describe pipelines where AI-generated content passes through a second, ostensibly independent evaluation step — a filter model deciding which candidate items survive, or blinded graders scoring which patches match — and the outcome correlates with which agent produced the content: filtered survivors disproportionately reflect the generating agent's own strengths/blind spots, and grader agreement rates differ specifically for an agent's own outputs versus others'. In both cases, the evaluation step fails to be neutral with respect to the content's origin, even though it was meant to be.
quote_1: one of our own agents wrote candidate bugs, a second model filtered the ones it judged too easy, and nobody checked whether the filter model shared blind spots with the author
quote_2: the evaluated agent agreed with external graders 6.4 points less often on its own successful patches than on matched patches from peers
